Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Diagnosis:
The test case `testUnionOfVariableAndNode` triggers an XPath evaluation on the expression "$var | /MAIN/A". This XPath is a union of a variable "$var" with a node set "/MAIN/A". The failure manifests as an exception from the method `NodePointer.compareNodePointers` with the following message: "Cannot compare pointers that do not belong to the same tree: '$var' and ''".

Inspecting the relevant method `NodePointer.compareNodePointers(NodePointer, int, NodePointer, int)` reveals that when two pointers are compared, the method first tries to adjust depths by recursively moving up parents. If at depth=1 the two pointers are not the same or related, the method throws the exception observed.

The error suggests that when union operation tries to order or compare pointers from two different node trees, specifically a pointer referring to a variable value and pointers referring to document nodes, the comparison does not succeed because variable pointers do not belong to the same node tree as document nodes (they are logically separate).

Therefore, the root cause is that comparing pointers from different "trees" or sources (variable vs document structure) is not supported by the existing implementation of `NodePointer.compareNodePointers`. Consequently, the union operation, which requires comparing all pointers to produce a resulting ordered set, throws an exception when it encounters variable pointers.

The recent bug reports are unrelated.

Summary: The bug occurs because `NodePointer.compareNodePointers` throws an exception when comparing pointers from different trees, which happens in union expressions involving both variable nodes and document nodes.

Next, the likely location to fix is in the logic involving pointer comparisons or in the handling of union expressions when pointers refer to different "trees" (variable vs document). Possibly add special treatment for variable pointers to avoid or handle cross-tree comparison or modify union evaluation for this case.

I suggest we further inspect the class(es) responsible for producing/handling pointers for variables and union evaluation to confirm.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
